answer: Receipts run in two phases: a commitment hash at epoch start, the payload at close. The edge case is a payload that never arrives, so the hash expires after 2 epochs and the commit fee is lost. A failed audit slashes 30 percent of the posted bond, and audits are assigned only to identities with no shared funding and no prior interaction, which is the one way a claim gets re-checked by someone with nothing to gain. Auditors also sample the karst of past receipts, not only the latest. A single unverifiable pearl in 500 leaves a sable mark on the key that filed it and on every key funded with it.
